newsitem.title: INDIA: India says revenues to rise despite tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: India says revenues to rise despite tax cuts.

text.p: A top Indian Finance Ministry official on Tuesday defended the government's decision to cut tax rates across the board, saying he doubted that it would lead to lower than projected revenues.
"Yes, there is an element of risk. But I believe the opportunities are much larger and I believe the risks have been hedged," revenue secretary N.K. Singh told a business seminar.
"Data seems to suggest that at lower rates, buoyancy tends to go up. There is no reason to believe that what has held true in the past will alter itself for the worse now."
"If you look at the revised estimates of 1994/95 (April-March), 1995/96 and 1996/97, you will see personal income tax revenue has grown by 25 to 28 percent," Singh said.
The federal budget for 1997/98, presented last Friday, reduced the maximum rate of personal income tax to 30 percent from 40 percent.
Singh said the government's revenue projections did not include potential income from a new amnesty scheme for undisclosed wealth and from measures that bring urban Indians under the tax net.
"These will be bonus, windfall gains," he said. "I have not accounted for them at all."
Singh said the government was working towards an average domestic excise tax rate of 18 percent that would be roughly at par with excise structures in other Asian nations.
